reviews.reason: Event reduction owns delta promotion and turn boundaries. Preserve its exhaustive match and ephemeral sidecars. Durable input/outbox records enter LiveState after acknowledged commit; ordinary streaming retains asynchronous appends. UI row projection remains a separate owner. Appender now excludes every ephemeral notification at its own API boundary; direct live and durable paths preserve the same sidecar/history separation. Transcript projection and update planning now live under the transcript entity; frame reduction is unchanged.

Current projection, incremental catch-up and full rebuild remain distinct recovery paths. The inert schema migration flag and branch are removed. JSONL remains authoritative; format-v2 cutover rebuilds a fresh projection offline and validates every row before activation.

Clearing replaces only frozen tool-result occurrences in the provider view. Canonical history, current-round call/result pairs and memory projection have distinct contracts; preserve them. Both provider adapters now have HTTP/SSE contract coverage; the shared failure label is provider-neutral. Request projection and clearing behavior remain unchanged.

Keep the cohesive lexer for Git and Cargo command classification. Filesystem authority, metadata revalidation and approval stay outside it. Passing dispatch occurrence through the web adapter changes neither permission policy nor lexer behavior. Retry bookkeeping now comes from contract rather than transcript; shell tokenization and approval capability decisions remain unchanged. Human and judge approvals now share only execution dispatch after their original validation. Shell classification and grant revalidation remain unchanged.

The frame layer now correlates required call and occurrence identities exactly; latest-preceding fallback is removed. This function owns tool and approval presentation, preserving request order, per-execution rows and source indices. Provider replay still answers one logical call across retries; that responsibility stays separate.

Keep the session loop as owner of command priority, environment readiness and provider/completion ordering. Appender now acknowledges durable input/outbox and recovery records before live folding, publication or resume. Async completions are admitted by dispatch occurrence. Task children and MoA watchers retain their distinct lifetimes. Initial capabilities are now installed through ToolSessionBuilder before sharing; shared wire conversion preserves ephemeral feedback without changing those ordering and lifetime rules. In-memory daemon fixtures now resolve no host settings; production session order and configuration loading are unchanged.

Excluded subpaths must deny writes before selecting the longest sufficient capability. Coverage, sufficient access and refusal evidence are separate decisions; preserve the ordered matcher. Linux and macOS wrappers now share cwd, environment and stdio preparation. Capability construction, helper protocol and path authorization remain unchanged.
Keep the OS-specific capability probe and the unsupported-platform false result. Syntactic cfg identity is tracked separately; only Linux execution and FreeBSD cross-compilation were verified.

Key and modifier combinations follow distinct wire encodings; preserve the protocol table and its mode-specific branches.

The select macro hides much of this state machine from function metrics. Preserve bounded PTY-query priority before keys/paste/text, synchronized-update deadlines, and latest-frame publication; encoding-only input must not consume the visible update slot. Normal output and timeout flushing share side-effect delivery while the loop retains priority and timing ownership. TerminalSize now applies engine minima at PTY/core entry; valid geometry and independent pixel dimensions are preserved. Channel pairs are now constructed inside terminal-core and shared by the host and tests. Receiver fields are internal; disconnecting either input owner still terminates the core, with the other input retained in regression coverage. Key, committed text and paste now share one ordered CoreInput FIFO after a GUI repro exposed cross-channel reordering. Bounded PTY-query priority, encoding-only notification behavior and paste notification remain unchanged. Terminal subscriber registration and failed-create cleanup now share attachment ownership; the core queue, snapshot and exit contracts are unchanged.

Key bindings map the internal CommandId vocabulary; CLI requests expose a different wire vocabulary. Preserve these tables instead of unifying distinct operation surfaces. The CLI request name is now read from its own external_name table instead of copied in request construction; internal and external command vocabularies remain distinct.

Directory watching survives artifact replacement, content filtering avoids reload loops, and dropping the owner cancels the quiet-period task. Preserve this watcher beside pane-owned load and receipt tasks. GPUI virtual-clock tests now exercise the real quiet-period loop across bursts and cancellation, replacing a constant-only timing assertion.

Character branches encode distinct geometry. Shared row shaping and text decorations now live in shaping.rs; geometry and cache epoch semantics remain unchanged. Paint/cache ownership moved to terminal/paint.rs; glyph geometry is unchanged.

Live and history painting have distinct cache indices and generations. Cursor, selection and IME belong to the live viewport; both paths use the same separately owned row shaping. Both paths now also share background painting, including empty-text colored spans. Painting now has its own module and reads preedit through KeyboardInput; live/history geometry and cache contracts are unchanged.

Color roles share one resolved seed and contrast policy. Preserve the cohesive derivation; live application and TOML persistence already have separate owners. The editor reuses the same contrast normalizer; config saving handles normal and inline TOML tables with errors for invalid shapes.
